title: HyperscalerProductionReadinessClaimContract
description: Claim ceiling and evidence contract for any Oyatie plan, ADR, spec, product, service, or toolchain surface that wants to say hyperscaler-grade, production-ready, mechanically enforced, secure, isolated, tenant-facing, retired, done, parity, full, automatic, or equivalent. The contract prevents false, empty, or aspirational promises by making claims tiered, evidence-backed, and mechanically gateable through cloud-ci/Rust gate crates rather than new oya CLI surfaces.

_meta.source_request: Founder refinement: hyperscaler-grade / production-ready / mechanically-enforced claims require specs befitting such claims; multi-year horizon favors doing it correctly over short delivery time.
non_negotiables: No new oya CLI surface. All new enforcement is Rust gate crates, cloud-ci/oya-ci required contexts, generated registries, or controllers.
Aspirational language is allowed only when labeled target/non-claim and paired with a path to evidence.
Mechanically enforced means branch-protected cloud-ci required context plus RED/GREEN fixtures, not local checks or operator procedure.
Production-ready and hyperscaler-grade are per-service/per-plane claims, not program-wide adjectives.
Sustained evidence matters: point-in-time design review is not production readiness.

claim_tiers.meaning: Architecture direction or desired end state only. Cannot be used as readiness, security, scale, enforcement, customer-facing, or completion proof.
The contract is concrete enough to implement and test, but not yet enforced or proven live.
A candidate change cannot merge while violating the invariant.
A service can safely serve real tenants within declared SLO, security, isolation, observability, operations, deployment, and recovery constraints.

A mature, measured, multi-cell/multi-region, highly automated platform/service operating with sustained evidence across reliability, security, release, tenant isolation, supply chain, capacity, and operational excellence. This is not a synonym for good architecture.

evidence_domains.name: Reliability and SLO/error-budget management
minimum_for_production_ready: release freeze or throttle rule on budget exhaustion
minimum_for_hyperscaler_grade: capacity and failover drills tied to SLOs

evidence_domains.name: Performance budgets and capacity evidence
minimum_for_production_ready: service-level latency budget with p50/p95/p99 and measurement window
throughput/concurrency budget for declared tenant tier
load and soak test report tied to the release candidate
cloud-ci performance regression guard for changed services or explicit exception packet
resource saturation dashboard and alert threshold
capacity breakpoint plus rollback/fail-shed decision rule
minimum_for_hyperscaler_grade: N+2 capacity model or documented equivalent by cell/region
peak-load or game-day capacity drill with dated results
continuous trend for p95/p99 latency, saturation, queue time, and error rate
autoscaling, admission-control, queuing, or fail-shed policy proven under load
cost/performance/sustainability trade-off review with closed high risks

evidence_domains.name: Release safety and rollback
minimum_for_hyperscaler_grade: config/feature-flag/IaC pipelines use the same safety model

evidence_domains.name: CI, merge admission, and mechanical enforcement
minimum_for_hyperscaler_grade: metrics for queue latency and failure causes

evidence_domains.name: Secure SDLC and supply chain
minimum_for_hyperscaler_grade: SLSA target level documented and verified

gates_to_build_without_oya_cli.type: Rust gate crate + cloud-ci required context
blocks_on: done/retired claim with live references outside a retirement packet

gates_to_build_without_oya_cli.type: Rust gate crate + cloud-ci required context or release-promotion context
blocks_on: production-ready or hyperscaler-grade claim without explicit performance budget
missing p95/p99/throughput/capacity measurement for changed service
performance regression without owner, expiry, and rollback/fail-shed exception packet
advisory-only benchmark presented as release authority
new oya CLI command or required-context producer

multi_year_closure_roadmap.outcome: No false/empty promises can enter authoritative plan/ADR/spec surfaces. Required evidence schemas, generated matrices, and RED/GREEN fixtures exist.
cloud-ci/oya-ci required contexts, Rust gates, Tide minimum, generated registries, and branch-protection mappings block violations. No oya CLI required-context producer remains.
At least one internal dogfood vertical meets production_ready tier in an isolated tenant/cell with SLOs, canary, rollback, tenant isolation, security, supply-chain, capacity, and DR evidence.
External tenant preview workloads meet production_ready tier; gaps are visible in claim-evidence map and cannot be marketed as hyperscaler-grade.

Selected services earn hyperscaler_grade tier only after sustained multi-cell/multi-region, SLO/error-budget, automated release, supply-chain, tenant-isolation, capacity, chaos, DR, and well-architected evidence over the required window.
